title: Pose from a description
description: Changes the pose of the person in picture 1 to the pose of the person in picture 2, by words only, and makes the pose fit picture 1's setting. A language model that reads images writes three texts: picture 1's setting without its subject (place, background, light, camera, mood, style), picture 2's body pose without its person, and what picture 2's pose stands, sits or leans on (stairs, a wall, a chair). A second, text-only step joins them into one edit instruction: keep the setting and the person, change the pose, and use what picture 1 really offers (a step, a rock, a bench, the ground) instead of props it lacks, so no limb floats in the air. FLUX.2 Klein 9B follows that instruction with picture 1 as its only reference and never sees picture 2. All four texts are shown, each prompt is a text field on its node so you can tune it, and Extra instructions adds your own wishes. The result is saved and shown against picture 1 in a Compare Images slider. Good at: keeping picture 1's scene and person, simple and medium poses. Weak at: poses that words describe badly (twisted torsos, crossed limbs), and a small model may leave a little of the subject in the setting text or invent a prop; read the texts and edit the prompts if so. Needs a language model that reads images. The sample pictures and the preview are those of Pose transfer, made with Fugue (Z-Image Turbo).
